<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">First quarter 2020:</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;">Geopolitical events that increased the supply of low-priced oil to the global market occurred at the same time that demand weakened due to the worldwide effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to a collapse in oil prices during March 2020.&#160;&#160;As a result, Schlumberger&#8217;s market capitalization deteriorated significantly compared to the end of 2019.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#8217;s stock price reached a low during the first quarter of 2020 not seen since 1995.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the Philadelphia Oil Services Sector index, which is comprised of companies involved in the oil services sector, reached an all-time low.&#160;&#160;As a result of these facts, Schlumberger determined that it was more likely than not that the fair value of certain of its reporting units were less than their carrying value.&#160;&#160;Therefore, Schlumberger performed an interim goodwill impairment test.</span></p></td></tr></table></div>
</ix:nonNumeric><p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">9</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" /><ix:continuation id="F_000436_dcnt_d88750c8-fe3e-4809-9775-9337fc0b7fcc" continuedAt="F_000436_dcnt_c10ae7d3-f239-4bc2-a2a1-2a927f2ddb7d">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger had <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000516" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200101_20200331" decimals="INF">11</ix:nonFraction> reporting units with goodwill balances aggregating $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000517" name="us-gaap:GoodwillGross" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">16.0</ix:nonFraction> billion.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger determined that the fair value of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000518" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbFourReportingUnitsMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">four</ix:nonFraction> of its reporting units, representing $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000519" name="us-gaap:GoodwillGross" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbFourReportingUnitsMember_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">4.5</ix:nonFraction> billion of the goodwill, was substantially in excess of their carrying value.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger performed a detailed quantitative impairment assessment of the remaining <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000520" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSevenReportingUnitsMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">seven</ix:nonFraction> reporting units, which represented $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000521" name="us-gaap:GoodwillGross" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSevenReportingUnitsMember_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">11.5</ix:nonFraction> billion of goodwill. As a result of this assessment, Schlumberger concluded that the goodwill associated with each of these seven reporting units was impaired, resulting in a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000522" name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetImpairment" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200101_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">3.1</ix:nonFraction> billion goodwill impairment charge.&#160;&#160;This charge primarily relates to goodwill associated with the Drilling and Production segments.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Following the $3.1 billion goodwill impairment charge relating to these seven reporting units, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000523" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSixReportingUnitsMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">six</ix:nonFraction> of these reporting units had a remaining goodwill balance.&#160;&#160;These six reporting units had goodwill balances which ranged between $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000524" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSixReportingUnitsMember_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">0.2</ix:nonFraction> billion and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000525" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSixReportingUnitsMember_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">5.0</ix:nonFraction> billion and aggregated to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000526" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSixReportingUnitsMember_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">8.4</ix:nonFraction> billion as of March 31, 2020. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger used the income approach to estimate the fair value of its reporting units, but also considered the market approach to validate the results.&#160;&#160;The income approach estimates the fair value by discounting each reporting unit&#8217;s estimated future cash flows using Schlumberger&#8217;s estimate of the discount rate, or expected return, that a marketplace participant would have required as of the valuation date.&#160;&#160;The market approach includes the use of comparative multiples to corroborate the discounted cash flow results.&#160;&#160;The market approach involves significant judgement involved in the selection of the appropriate peer group companies and valuation multiples.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Some of the more significant assumptions inherent in the income approach include the estimated future net annual cash flows for each reporting unit and the discount rate.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger selected the assumptions used in the discounted cash flow projections using historical data supplemented by current and anticipated market conditions and estimated growth rates.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#8217;s estimates are based upon assumptions believed to be reasonable.&#160;&#160;However, given the inherent uncertainty in determining the assumptions underlying a discounted cash flow analysis, particularly in the current volatile market, actual results may differ from those used in Schlumberger&#8217;s valuations which could result in additional impairment charges in the future.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The discount rates utilized to value Schlumberger&#8217;s reporting units were between <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000527" name="slb:DiscountRateUtilized" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="3" scale="-2">12.0</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000528" name="slb:DiscountRateUtilized" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="3" scale="-2">13.5</ix:nonFraction>%, depending on the risks and uncertainty inherent in the respective reporting unit as well as the size of the reporting unit.&#160;&#160;Assuming all other assumptions and inputs used in each of the respective discounted cash flow analysis were held constant, a <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000529" name="slb:ExpectedIncreaseDecreaseInDiscountRateAssumption" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200101_20200331" decimals="4" scale="-4">50</ix:nonFraction>-basis point increase or decrease in the discount rate assumptions would have changed the fair value of the <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000530" name="slb:NumberOfReportingUnitsFairValueToBeImpacted" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200101_20200331" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">seven</ix:nonFraction> reporting units, on average, by less than <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000531" name="slb:ExpectedPercentageChangeInFairValueOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="2" scale="-2">5</ix:nonFraction>%.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the second quarter of 2020, Schlumberger established a &#8364;<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217EUR" id="F_000836" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebtNoncurrent" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_slbGuaranteedEuroMediumTermNoteProgramMember_20200630" decimals="-8" scale="9">5.0</ix:nonFraction> billion Guaranteed Euro Medium Term Note program that provides for the issuance of various types of debt instruments such as fixed or floating rate notes in euro, US dollar or other currencies.&#160; Schlumberger has not issued any debt under this program.</p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger Limited fully and unconditionally guarantees the securities issued by certain of its subsidiaries, including securities issued by Schlumberger Investment SA, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Schlumberger.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000444" name="us-gaap:DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200101_20200630" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000444_dcnt_9e68e5fa-4700-451d-a130-84ae80eb1b72">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">10.&#160;&#160; <span style="text-decoration:underline;">Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities</span> </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is exposed to market risks related to fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates and interest rates.&#160; To mitigate these risks, Schlumberger utilizes derivative instruments.&#160; Schlumberger does not enter into derivative transactions for speculative purposes. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Interest Rate Risk </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is subject to interest rate risk on its debt and its investment portfolio.&#160; Schlumberger maintains an interest rate risk management strategy that uses a mix of variable and fixed rate debt combined with its investment portfolio, to mitigate the exposure to changes in interest rates.&#160; </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At June 30, 2020, Schlumberger had fixed rate debt aggregating $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000837" name="slb:FixedRateDebt" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200630" decimals="-8" scale="9">15.5</ix:nonFraction> billion and variable rate debt aggregating $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000838" name="slb:VariableRateDebt" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200630" decimals="-8" scale="9">1.9</ix:nonFraction> billion. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Foreign Currency Exchange Rate Risk </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As a multinational company, Schlumberger generates revenue in more than <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbCountry" id="F_000839" name="us-gaap:NumberOfCountriesInWhichEntityOperates" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200630" decimals="INF">120</ix:nonFraction> countries. Schlumberger&#8217;s functional currency is primarily the US dollar.&#160; However, outside the United States, a significant portion of Schlumberger&#8217;s expenses are incurred in foreign currencies.&#160; Therefore, when the US dollar weakens (strengthens) in relation to the foreign currencies of the countries in which Schlumberger conducts business, the US dollar-reported expenses will increase (decrease).&#160;&#160; </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is exposed to risks on future cash flows to the extent that the local currency is not the functional currency and expenses denominated in local currency are not equal to revenues denominated in local currency.&#160; Schlumberger uses foreign currency forward contracts to provide a hedge against a portion of these cash flow risks.&#160; These contracts are accounted for as cash flow hedges, with the changes in the fair value of the hedge recorded on the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Balance Sheet </span>and in <span style="font-style:italic;">Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss.&#160; </span>Amounts recorded in<span style="font-style:italic;"> Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss </span>are reclassified into earnings in the same period or periods that the hedged item is recognized in earnings.&#160; </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is also exposed to risks on future cash flows relating to certain of its fixed rate debt denominated in currencies other than the functional currency. Schlumberger uses cross-currency swaps to provide a hedge against these cash flow risks. </p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is exposed to changes in the fair value of assets and liabilities that are denominated in currencies other than the functional currency.&#160; While Schlumberger uses foreign currency forward contracts and foreign currency options to economically hedge this exposure as it relates to certain currencies, these contracts are not designated as hedges for accounting purposes.&#160; Instead, the fair value of the contracts is recorded on the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Balance Sheet, </span>and changes in the fair value are recognized in the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Statement of Income (Loss) </span>as are changes in fair value of the hedged item.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At June 30, 2020, contracts were outstanding for the US dollar equivalent of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000887" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapDerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis_us-gaapForeignExchangeContractMember_20200630" decimals="INF" scale="9">9.8</ix:nonFraction> billion in various foreign currencies, of which $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000888" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapDerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis_us-gaapForeignExchangeContractMember_us-gaapFinancialInstrumentAxis_us-gaapDebtMember_us-gaapHedgingDesignationAxis_us-gaapDesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember_20200630" decimals="INF" scale="9">6.0</ix:nonFraction> billion relates to hedges of debt denominated in currencies other than the functional currency. </p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is party to various legal proceedings from time to time.&#160;&#160;A liability is accrued when a loss is both probable and can be reasonably estimated.&#160;&#160;Management believes that the probability of a material loss with respect to any currently pending legal proceeding is remote.&#160;&#160;However, litigation is inherently uncertain and it is not possible to predict the ultimate disposition of any of these proceedings.&#160;&#160; </p></ix:nonNumeric>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Due to the actions taken by Schlumberger to reduce its global workforce during 2020, Schlumberger experienced a significant reduction in the expected aggregate years of future service of its employees in its US postretirement medical plan. Accordingly, Schlumberger recorded a curtailment gain of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001172" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanRecognizedNetGainLossDueToSettlementsAndCurtailments1" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapIncomeStatementLocationAxis_slbImpairmentAndOtherMember_us-gaapRetirementPlanTypeAxis_us-gaapDefinedBenefitPostretirementHealthCoverageMember_20200401_20200630" decimals="-6" scale="6">69</ix:nonFraction> million during the second quarter of 2020 relating to this plan. The curtailment gain includes recognition of the decrease in the benefit obligation as well as a portion of the previously unrecognized prior service credit, reflecting the reduction in expected years of future service.&#160; As a result of the curtailment, Schlumberger performed a remeasurement of the plan, which had an immaterial impact.&#160; This gain was classified in <span style="font-style:italic;">Impairments &#38; other</span> in the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Statement of Income (Loss)</span>.&#160; See Note 2 &#8211; <span style="font-style:italic;">Charge and Credits</span>.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">(3)</sup></span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">Interest expense excludes amounts which are included in the segments&#8217; income ($7 million in Q2 2020&#59; $7 million in Q1 2020).</p></td></tr></table></div>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:4.54%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">(4)</sup></span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">Charges and credits are described in detail in Note 2 to the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Financial Statements.</span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The second quarter of 2020 was probably the most challenging quarter in past decades. Second-quarter revenue of $5.4 billion declined 28% sequentially, caused by the significant decrease in North America activity, and international activity drop due to downward revisions to customer budgets accentuated by COVID-19 disruptions. The entire oil and gas industry was confronted with historic oil demand and supply imbalances caused by demand destruction from the global COVID-19 containment effort. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">North America revenue declined 48% sequentially with land revenue falling 60% as customers dramatically cut back spending. International revenue declined 19% sequentially with Latin America and Africa experiencing the largest revenue declines due to COVID-19-related restrictions and the drop in deepwater activity. In addition, there was a production interruption in the Asset Performance Solutions (&#8220;APS&#8221;) projects in Ecuador caused by a major landslide that led to the rupture of the main pipeline.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger has worked to protect its liquidity and cash positions and sustained resilient international margins while navigating the trough of this downcycle. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Despite the severe drop in international revenue and the effect of the APS production interruption in Ecuador, international margin was essentially flat compared to the previous quarter, due to Schlumberger&#8217;s swift and decisive actions to reduce operating costs, restructure, and rationalize its asset base. Schlumberger is working to permanently remove $1.5 billion of structural costs annually by reorganizing into a leaner and more responsive company that is better aligned with its customers&#8217; workflows. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Looking at the macro view in the near-term, during the beginning of the third quarter of 2020 oil demand slowly started to normalize and is expected to continue to improve as government measures support consumption. However, subsequent waves of potential COVID-19 resurgence pose a negative risk to this outlook. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The conditions are set in the third quarter for a modest frac completion activity increase in North America, though from a very low base. Internationally, markets may continue to be disrupted by the pandemic and will continue to adjust to budget levels set during the second quarter, but this is expected to be mostly offset if there is a seasonal return of activity in the Northern Hemisphere and a rebound of Latin America from its second-quarter weakness. However, any further material COVID-19 disruption or significant setback in oil demand arising from a slower economic recovery could present downside risks to this outlook. Absent these risks, Schlumberger anticipates flat sequential revenue in the third quarter. Schlumberger expects its third quarter pretax segment operating income and margin to expand as a result of its restructuring efforts, improved activity mix, and sustained benefits from technology adoption, including digital.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">21</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Characterization </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Characterization revenue of $1.1 billion decreased 20% sequentially. This was mainly due to lower Wireline activity in North America land and the Eastern Middle East and Sub-Sahara Africa GeoMarkets. Testing Services revenue was also lower mainly in the Sub-Sahara Africa GeoMarket as a result of projects that were completed in the prior quarter, as well as delayed and cancelled activities due to COVID-19.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Characterization pretax operating margin of 18% rebounded 357 bps sequentially despite the significant revenue decline. This margin expansion was driven by prompt cost reduction measures through headcount rationalization and furloughs.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Drilling </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Drilling revenue of $1.7 billion decreased 24% sequentially. This was primarily due to the activity decline in US land as rig count dropped more than 50%, while COVID-19 disruptions caused drilling activities to be cancelled or suspended in several international GeoMarkets. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Drilling pretax operating margin of 10% contracted by 289 bps sequentially. Drilling &#38; Measurements and M-I SWACO accounted for most of the margin decline and experienced the largest drop in activity due to their sizeable footprint in North America land.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production revenue of $1.6 billion decreased 40% sequentially. This was driven by the sharp drop in OneStim<sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> pressure-pumping activity in North America land, lower APS revenue due primarily to the significant production interruption in Ecuador and COVID-19 disruptions.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production pretax operating margin of 2% contracted by 630 bps sequentially.&#160;&#160;The margin decline was due to reduced profitability in North America land from the dramatic fall in activity, which mostly impacted the OneStim margin, as well as the drop in APS revenue in Ecuador.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cameron </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cameron revenue of $1.0 billion decreased 19% sequentially. The decline was driven by lower Surface Systems and Valves &#38; Process Systems revenues in North America and lower Drilling Systems sales. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cameron pretax operating margin of 8% declined by 180 bps sequentially primarily due to the significant revenue decline.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">22</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Second</span><span style="text-decoration:underline;"> Quarter 20</span><span style="text-decoration:underline;">20</span><span style="text-decoration:underline;"> Compared to </span><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Second</span><span style="text-decoration:underline;"> </span><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Quarter 20</span><span style="text-decoration:underline;">19</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">(3)</sup></span></p></td>

<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:4.54%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">(4)</sup></span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">Charges and credits are described in detail in Note 2 to the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Financial Statements.</span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Second-quarter 2020 revenue of $5.4 billion was 35% lower compared to the same period last year due to the significant fall in North America activity,  well as the international activity drop due to downward revisions to customer budgets accentuated by COVID-19 disruptions. With market uncertainty weighing on demand outlook, North America revenue declined 58% reflecting the continued capital discipline of North America operators, who reduced drilling and frac activity. International revenue decreased 24%.&#160;&#160;This decline was most prominent in Latin America and Africa due to COVID-19-related restrictions and the drop in deepwater activity, as well as the effect of the APS production interruption in Ecuador. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Characterization </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Second-quarter 2020 revenue of $1.1 billion decreased 32% year-on-year.&#160; This was mainly due to lower Wireline and WesternGeco revenue as customers pulled back activity due to COVID-19 and cut discretionary spending and exploration in several international GeoMarkets. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 273 bps to 18% due to reduced profitability, largely in Wireline and WesternGeco.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Drilling </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Second-quarter 2020 revenue of $1.7 billion decreased 28% year-on-year. This was primarily due to the activity decline in US land as rig count significantly decreased, while COVID-19 disruptions caused drilling activities to be cancelled or suspended in several international GeoMarkets. Revenue was also lower due to the divestiture of the Drilling Tools businesses at the end of the fourth quarter of 2019.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#FF0000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 288 bps to 10% due to the significant reduction in activity in North America.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Second-quarter 2020 revenue of $1.6 billion decreased 48% year-on-year. This revenue decrease was driven by the sharp drop in OneStim pressure pumping activity in North America land, lower APS revenue due primarily to the significant production interruption in Ecuador and COVID-19 disruptions.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">23</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 612 bps to 2% due primarily to reduced profitability in OneStim in North America land.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cameron </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:8pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Second-quarter 2020 revenue of $1.0 billion decreased 24% year-on-year. The decline was driven primarily by lower Valves &#38; Process Systems and Surface Systems revenue in North America. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:8pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 453 bps to 8% due to the significant revenue decline.</p>

<td valign="top">

<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:4.54%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">(2)</sup></span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">Interest income excludes amounts which are included in the segments&#8217; income ($1 million in 2020&#59; $5 million in 2019). </p></td></tr></table></div>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:4.54%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">(3)</sup></span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">Interest expense excludes amounts which are included in the segments&#8217; income ($15 million in 2020&#59; $20 million in 2019).</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">(4)</sup>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Charges and credits are described in detail in Note 2 to the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Financial Statements.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Six-month 2020 revenue of $12.8 billion was 21% lower compared to the same period last year due to the significant fall in North America activity, as well as the international activity drop due to downward revisions to customer budgets accentuated by COVID-19 disruptions. With market uncertainty weighing on demand outlook, North America revenue declined 37% reflecting the continued capital discipline of North America operators, who reduced drilling and frac activity. International revenue decreased 12%. The decline was most prominent in Latin America and Africa due to COVID-19 related restrictions and the drop in deepwater activity, as well as the effect of the APS production interruption in Ecuador. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Characterization </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Six-month 2020 revenue of $2.4 billion decreased 22% year-on-year. This was mainly due to lower Wireline and WesternGeco revenue as customers pulled back activity due to COVID-19 and cut discretionary spending and exploration in several international GeoMarkets. Testing Services and Software Integrated Solutions revenue declined slightly.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 421 bps to 16% due to reduced profitability largely in Wireline and WesternGeco.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Drilling </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Six-month 2020 revenue of $4.0 billion decreased 16% year-on-year. This was primarily due to the activity decline in US land as rig count significantly decreased while COVID-19 disruptions caused drilling activities to be cancelled or suspended in several </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">24</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">international GeoMarkets. Revenue was also lower due to the divestiture of the Drilling Tools businesses at the end of the fourth quarter of 2019.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#FF0000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 145 bps to 11%.&#160; Margins were lower due to the decrease in revenue and COVID-19-related disruptions.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Six-month 2020 revenue of $4.3 billion decreased 28% year-on-year. This revenue decrease was driven primarily by the sharp drop in OneStim pressure pumping activity in North America land, lower APS revenue due primarily to the significant production interruption in Ecuador and COVID-19 disruptions.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 211 bps to 5% due primarily to reduced profitability in OneStim in North America land.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cameron </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:8pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Six-month 2020 revenue of $2.3 billion decreased 12% year-on-year. The decline was driven primarily by lower Valves &#38; Process Systems and Surface Systems revenue in North America.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:8pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 322 bps to 9% due to the significant revenue decline.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Interest and Other Income</span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The effective tax rate for the second quarter of 2020 was 6%, as compared to 17% for the same period of 2019.&#160;&#160;The charges described in Note 2 to the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Financial Statements</span> reduced the effective tax rate for the second quarter of 2020 by 17 percentage points as a significant portion of these charges were not tax-effective.&#160;&#160;Changes in the geographic mix of pretax earnings increased the effective tax rate for the second quarter of 2020 by six percentage points as compared to the same period of 2019.&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The effective tax rate for first six months of 2020 was 8% as compared to 16% for the same period of 2019.&#160;&#160;The charges described in Note 2 to the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Financial Statements</span> reduced the effective tax rate for the first six months of 2020 by 10 percentage points as a significant portion of these charges were not tax-effective.&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">25</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The first quarter 2020 results did not include any benefit from reduced depreciation and amortization expense as a result of the first quarter impairment charges.&#160; However, commencing with the second quarter of 2020, depreciation and amortization expense was reduced by approximately $95 million on a quarterly basis as a result of the first quarter impairment charges.&#160;&#160;Approximately $45 million of this quarterly reduction is reflected in the Production segment, with the remaining $50 million reflected in the &#8220;Corporate &#38; other&#8221; line item. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The second quarter 2020 results did not include any benefit from reduced expenses associated with the second quarter restructuring and impairment charges. However, going forward depreciation and amortization expense will be reduced by approximately $80 million and lease expense will be reduced by $25 million, on a quarterly basis.&#160;&#160;Approximately $70 million of this quarterly reduction will be reflected in the Production Segment, with the remaining $35 million reflected amongst the Reservoir Characterization, Drilling and Cameron segments. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There were no charges or credits recorded during the first six months of 2019.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Liquidity and Capital Resources</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The <span style="color:#000000;">effects of the COVID-19 pandemic have resulted in a significant and swift reduction in international and U.S. economic activity. These effects have adversely affected the demand for oil and natural gas, as well as for Schlumberger&#8217;s products and services, and </span>caused significant volatility and disruption of the financial markets. This period of extreme economic disruption, low oil prices and reduced demand for Schlumberger&#8217;s products and services has had, and is likely to continue to have, a material adverse impact on Schlumberger&#8217;s business, results of operations, financial condition and, at times, access to sources of liquidity. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In view of the uncertainty of the depth and extent of the contraction in oil demand due to the COVID-19 pandemic combined with the weaker commodity price environment, Schlumberger has turned its strategic focus to cash conservation and protecting its balance sheet. As a result, in April 2020 Schlumberger announced a 75% reduction to its quarterly dividend. The revised dividend supports Schlumberger&#8217;s value proposition through a balanced approach of shareholder distributions and organic investment, while providing the flexibility to weather the uncertain environment. This decision reflects the Company&#8217;s focus on its capital stewardship program as well as its commitment to maintain both a strong liquidity position and a strong investment grade credit rating that provides privileged access to the financial markets.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">26</p>

Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">For quantitative and qualitative disclosures about market risk affecting Schlumberger, see Item&#160;7A, &#8220;Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk,&#8221; of the Schlumberger Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December&#160;31, 2019. Schlumberger&#8217;s exposure to market risk has not changed materially since December&#160;31, 2019.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Item_4_Controls_and_Procedures"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;4. Controls and Procedures. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger has carried out an evaluation under the supervision and with the participation of Schlumberger&#8217;s management, including the Chief Executive Officer (&#8220;CEO&#8221;) and the Chief Financial Officer (&#8220;CFO&#8221;), of the effectiveness of Schlumberger&#8217;s &#8220;disclosure controls and procedures&#8221; (as such term is defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;)) as of the end of the period covered by this report. Based on this evaluation, the CEO and the CFO have concluded that, as of the end of the period covered by this report, Schlumberger&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures were effective to provide reasonable assurance that information required to be disclosed in the reports that Schlumberger files or submits under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the Securities and Exchange Commission&#8217;s rules and forms. Schlumberger&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures include controls and procedures designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in reports filed or submitted under the Exchange Act is accumulated and communicated to its management, including the CEO and the CFO, as appropriate, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure. There was no change in Schlumberger&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting during the quarter to which this report relates that has materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, Schlumberger&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Item_4_Mine_Safety_Disclosures"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;4. Mine Safety Disclosures. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our mining operations are subject to regulation by the federal Mine Safety and Health Administration under the Federal Mine Safety and Health Act of 1977. Information concerning mine safety violations or other regulatory matters required by section 1503(a) of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act and Item&#160;104 of Regulation S-K is included in Exhibit 95 to this report.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Item_5_Other_Information"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;5. Other Information. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In 2013, Schlumberger completed the wind down of its service operations in Iran. Prior to this, certain non-US subsidiaries provided oilfield services to the National Iranian Oil Company and certain of its affiliates (&#8220;NIOC&#8221;).</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger&#8217;s residual transactions or dealings with the government of Iran during the second quarter of 2020 consisted of payments of taxes and other typical governmental charges. Certain non-US subsidiaries of Schlumberger maintain depository accounts at the Dubai branch of Bank Saderat Iran (&#8220;Saderat&#8221;), and at Bank Tejarat (&#8220;Tejarat&#8221;) in Tehran and in Kish for the deposit by NIOC of amounts owed to non-US subsidiaries of Schlumberger for prior services rendered in Iran and for the maintenance of such amounts previously received. One non-US subsidiary also maintained an account at Tejarat for payment of local expenses such as taxes. Schlumberger anticipates that it will discontinue dealings with Saderat and Tejarat following the receipt of all amounts owed to Schlumberger for prior services rendered in Iran.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">30</p>

<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">Amounts included are the total dollar value of proposed assessments received from MSHA during the quarter on or before June 30, 2020, regardless of whether the assessment has been challenged or appealed.&nbsp;&nbsp;Citations and orders can be contested and appealed, and as part of that process, are sometimes reduced in severity and amount, and sometimes dismissed.&nbsp;&nbsp;The number of citations, orders, and proposed assessments vary by inspector and vary depending on the size and type of the operation.</p></td></tr></table></div>

&lt;p style="text-align:right;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;11,230&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="background-color:#FFFFFF;padding-left:0pt;padding-Right:0.75pt;padding-Top:0.75pt;width:1%; border-bottom:double 2.5pt transparent;white-space:nowrap;" valign="bottom"&gt;
&lt;p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;color:#000000;font-size:1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;

&lt;/table&gt;&lt;/div&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;First quarter 2020:&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;div style="align:left;"&gt;
&lt;table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;"&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap" valign="top"&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap" valign="top"&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td valign="top"&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Times New Roman;"&gt;Geopolitical events that increased the supply of low-priced oil to the global market occurred at the same time that demand weakened due to the worldwide effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to a collapse in oil prices during March 2020.&#160;&#160;As a result, Schlumberger&#x2019;s market capitalization deteriorated significantly compared to the end of 2019.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#x2019;s stock price reached a low during the first quarter of 2020 not seen since 1995.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the Philadelphia Oil Services Sector index, which is comprised of companies involved in the oil services sector, reached an all-time low.&#160;&#160;As a result of these facts, Schlumberger determined that it was more likely than not that the fair value of certain of its reporting units were less than their carrying value.&#160;&#160;Therefore, Schlumberger performed an interim goodwill impairment test.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Schlumberger had 11 reporting units with goodwill balances aggregating $16.0 billion.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger determined that the fair value of four of its reporting units, representing $4.5 billion of the goodwill, was substantially in excess of their carrying value.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger performed a detailed quantitative impairment assessment of the remaining seven reporting units, which represented $11.5 billion of goodwill. As a result of this assessment, Schlumberger concluded that the goodwill associated with each of these seven reporting units was impaired, resulting in a $3.1 billion goodwill impairment charge.&#160;&#160;This charge primarily relates to goodwill associated with the Drilling and Production segments.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Following the $3.1 billion goodwill impairment charge relating to these seven reporting units, six of these reporting units had a remaining goodwill balance.&#160;&#160;These six reporting units had goodwill balances which ranged between $0.2 billion and $5.0 billion and aggregated to $8.4 billion as of March 31, 2020. &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Schlumberger used the income approach to estimate the fair value of its reporting units, but also considered the market approach to validate the results.&#160;&#160;The income approach estimates the fair value by discounting each reporting unit&#x2019;s estimated future cash flows using Schlumberger&#x2019;s estimate of the discount rate, or expected return, that a marketplace participant would have required as of the valuation date.&#160;&#160;The market approach includes the use of comparative multiples to corroborate the discounted cash flow results.&#160;&#160;The market approach involves significant judgement involved in the selection of the appropriate peer group companies and valuation multiples.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Some of the more significant assumptions inherent in the income approach include the estimated future net annual cash flows for each reporting unit and the discount rate.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger selected the assumptions used in the discounted cash flow projections using historical data supplemented by current and anticipated market conditions and estimated growth rates.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#x2019;s estimates are based upon assumptions believed to be reasonable.&#160;&#160;However, given the inherent uncertainty in determining the assumptions underlying a discounted cash flow analysis, particularly in the current volatile market, actual results may differ from those used in Schlumberger&#x2019;s valuations which could result in additional impairment charges in the future.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;The discount rates utilized to value Schlumberger&#x2019;s reporting units were between 12.0% and 13.5%, depending on the risks and uncertainty inherent in the respective reporting unit as well as the size of the reporting unit.&#160;&#160;Assuming all other assumptions and inputs used in each of the respective discounted cash flow analysis were held constant, a 50-basis point increase or decrease in the discount rate assumptions would have changed the fair value of the seven reporting units, on average, by less than 5%.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;div style="align:left;"&gt;
&lt;table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;"&gt;

&lt;p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;The estimate&lt;span style="font-size:10pt;"&gt;d fair value of Schlumberger&#x2019;s &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;"&gt;Long-term Debt, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:10pt;"&gt;based on quoted market prices at June 30, 2020 and December 31, 2019, was $17.3 billion and $15.3 billion, respectively.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During the second quarter of 2020, Schlumberger entered into a &#x20ac;1.54 billion committed revolving credit facility.&#160;&#160;This &lt;span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000804"&gt;one-year&lt;/span&gt; facility can be extended at Schlumberger&#x2019;s option for up to an additional year.&#160;&#160;No amounts have been drawn under this facility&lt;span style="font-size:12pt;"&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;At June 30, 2020, Schlumberger had separate committed credit facility agreements aggregating $7.98 billion with commercial banks, of which $6.17 billion was available and unused. &#160;These committed facilities support commercial paper programs in the United States and Europe, of which $1.73 billion matures in April 2021, $2.75 billion matures in February 2023, $1.5 billion matures in July 2024 and $2.0 billion matures in February 2025.&#160;&#160;Interest rates and other terms of borrowing under these lines of credit vary by facility.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Borrowings under the commercial paper programs at June 30, 2020 were $1.81 billion, all of which&#160;was classified in&#160;&lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Long-term debt&lt;/span&gt; in the &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Consolidated Balance &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;"&gt;Sheet&lt;/span&gt;.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2019, borrowings under the commercial paper programs were $2.22 billion, all of which was classified in &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Long-term debt&lt;/span&gt; in the &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Consolidated Balance Sheet&lt;/span&gt;.  &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During the first quarter of 2020, Schlumberger issued &#x20ac;400 million of 0.25% Notes due 2027 and &#x20ac;400 million of 0.50% Notes due 2031.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During the second quarter of 2020, Schlumberger issued &#x20ac;1.0 billion of 1.375% Guaranteed Notes due 2026, $900 million of 2.65% Senior Notes due 2030 and &#x20ac;1.0 billion of 2.00% Guaranteed Notes due 2032.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During the second quarter of 2020, Schlumberger repurchased all $600 million of its 4.20% Senior Notes due 2021 and $935 million of its 3.30% Senior Notes due 2021.&#160; Schlumberger paid a premium of approximately $40 million in connection with these repurchases.&#160; This premium was classified in &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Impairments &amp;amp; other&lt;/span&gt; in the &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Consolidated Statement of Income (Loss)&lt;/span&gt;.&#160; See Note 2 &#x2013; &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Charge and Credits&lt;/span&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
